title: Prime-to-characteristic bound for finite abelian characters
statement: Let $A$ be a finite abelian group, written multiplicatively, of order $n\ge1$, and let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Write $p=\operatorname{char}(k)$. If $p>0$, put $n'$ equal to the largest divisor of $n$ relatively prime to $p$; if $p=0$, put $n'=n$. Let $X=\operatorname{Hom}(A,k^\times)$ be the group of group homomorphisms, with multiplication $(\chi\psi)(a)=\chi(a)\psi(a)$. Then $X$ is finite and $$|X|\le n'.$$ No assumption that $k$ contains primitive roots of unity is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-abelian-cyclic-product] to choose $A\simeq\prod_{i\in I}\mathbf Z/d_i\mathbf Z$ with $I$ finite and $d_i>1$. Let $g_i\in A$ correspond to the tuple with entry $1\bmod d_i$ in coordinate $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. Thus $g_i^{d_i}=1$, and every $a\in A$ is $\prod_i g_i^{b_i}$ for representatives $0\le b_i<d_i$. Counting the tuples gives $n=\prod_i d_i$.

In characteristic zero put $m_i=d_i$. In positive characteristic, $p$ is prime: $p
eq1$ because $1_k
eq0$ [def-weil-field], and a factorization $p=uv$ with $1<u,v<p$ would give $(u\cdot1_k)(v\cdot1_k)=0$ although neither factor is zero, contradicting the field property [def-weil-field]. Factor $d_i=p^{a_i}m_i$ with $a_i\ge0$, $m_i\ge1$ and $p
mid m_i$. The product is $n=p^{\sum_i a_i}\prod_i m_i$, with $\prod_i m_i$ coprime to $p$. Hence $\prod_i m_i=n'$: it divides $n$ and is coprime to $p$, and any divisor of $n$ coprime to $p$ divides $\prod_i m_i$ by cancellation of the coprime factor $p^{\sum_i a_i}$. In characteristic zero the same equality follows from $n'=n$.

proof.text: For every character $\chi$, $\chi(g_i)^{d_i}=\chi(g_i^{d_i})=1$. In positive characteristic [lem-trf-roots-of-unity-remove-characteristic-power] applied to $a_i,m_i$ implies $\chi(g_i)^{m_i}=1$; in characteristic zero this already holds since $m_i=d_i$. Consequently evaluation gives a map $$X\longrightarrow\prod_i\mu_{m_i}(k),\qquad\chi\longmapsto(\chi(g_i))_i.$$ It is injective: if two characters agree on all $g_i$, then for every tuple of representatives $(b_i)$ they both take $\prod_i g_i^{b_i}$ to the same product $\prod_i\chi(g_i)^{b_i}$. These products exhaust $A$ by Step 1.

proof.text: Each $m_i\ge1$, so [lem-exc-field-roots-cyclic-bound] makes $\mu_{m_i}(k)$ finite with at most $m_i$ elements. Its finite product therefore has at most $\prod_i m_i=n'$ elements: list the choices in each coordinate and multiply their numbers. The injection in Step 3 identifies $X$ with a subset of this finite set, proving finiteness and $|X|\le n'$. If $I$ is empty the product is a singleton and $n=n'=1$, so this also covers the trivial group.
